product: DockLark, arrival warnings for refrigerated grocery routes

flaws.cause: The plan uses advance warnings to reduce failed evening handoffs. The route study establishes that managers already know arrival times and that receiving shifts end before vehicles can arrive. Better notices do not supply staff or change that time conflict, so the proposed service cannot reach its delivery goal.

evidence.what: Twenty-six of twenty-nine failures occur after receiving shifts end; arrival times are already known and neither shifts nor release times can change under current arrangements.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Replace notice-led intervention with an offer that changes receiving availability, holding arrangements, or funded timing.
flaws.fix: Design and test a service that bridges the staffed-hours gap, rather than treating awareness as the cause of missed handoffs.

flaws.cause: The first purchase decision occurs after twelve weeks of construction. The investment note identifies willingness to pay as the largest commercial uncertainty, and a cheap manual desk trial can test that exact price before the build. Most of the funded effort is spent before learning whether the buyer will purchase.

evidence.what: Finance directors control purchase and have neither reviewed the price nor assigned a budget.
A three-week manual paid trial is available before construction; willingness to pay is the largest uncertainty and builders cost $58,000.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Run the paid desk service first and authorize custom software only after finance directors demonstrate purchase acceptance.
flaws.fix: Move the priced manual trial ahead of hiring and construction, with a purchase threshold for funding the build.

notes: Changing the handoff mechanism does not establish purchase acceptance, and learning willingness to pay does not create staffed receiving hours.
